one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-05 has no Broadcom print: Q4 FY26 is reported after the close on Wed 2026-12-09 [2]. AVGO closed $377.32, +4.1% on the day (Oct 5 close $362.51 [17]) and +9.8% from the Oct 1 close of $343.64 [17]; the same-day move was reported as sympathy with Marvell's investor-day custom-silicon pitch [9] (context only, no company news). In-window events are sector/macro: Big-4 hyperscaler Q3 calls in late October with the first numeric 2027 capex guides (every 2026 guide went up per the house capex file [20], so a mild positive skew that is widely expected); the October FOMC with a cut priced at 0.5% (Polymarket, vol $211.5k) [14] and the 10y at 5.31% [15], so no rate relief; Anthropic IPO only 1.4% by Oct-31 and 13% by Nov-15 but 65.5% by Nov-30 [12], so mostly just after the window. Short-horizon base rate after a ~10% four-day run on read-through is partial reversal roughly offsetting momentum. Ladder: lognormal centred on $378.4 (+0.3% drift), monthly sigma 47%/3.5 = 13.4%, with 15% weight on a 1.6x-sigma component to fatten both tails (estimate).

fair_value.method: 0.6 x P/E (bottom-up FY28 EPS $23.92 x 19x = $454.5) + 0.4 x equity-FCF DCF at 12% ($274.6) = $382.5 -> $382. FY28 EPS rebuilt bottom-up: AI $177B (mean of three anchors: constant 2027 capex share $140.9B, purchase-commitment ratio $159.3B, management $230B) + non-AI $18.2B + software $36.2B = $231.5B revenue at 62% operating margin.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 (Nov-2027 to Oct-2028, the NTM year at the horizon) non-GAAP EPS $23.92 x 19x = $454.5

inputs_detail.derivation: Hock Tan: 'In 2027 we have secured the supply to again double AI revenue to approximately $115 billion.'

inputs_detail.input: FY28 AI revenue anchor 1: constant share of customer capex
inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 share 115/1,841 = 6.25% of 2027 ex-China base capex, applied to 2028 base $2,255B: 0.0625 x 2,255 = $140.9B.

inputs_detail.input: FY28 AI revenue anchor 2: purchase-commitment ratio
inputs_detail.derivation: $115B x ($72,952M FY28 / $52,674M FY27 purchase commitments) = $115B x 1.385 = $159.3B. FY28 commitments a year out are likely incomplete, so this leans low; a year earlier total commitments were only $235M [5], so there is no history to calibrate the ratio.

'We have line of sight for fiscal 2028 AI semiconductor revenue growth to again double to $230 billion.' Backed by GW line of sight: Anthropic +5 GW (2027) and +10 GW (2028), OpenAI 1.3 GW (2027) and >5 GW (2028).
Q4 guide ~$4.3B x 4 = $17.2B, grown 3%/yr for two years (judgment; Q4 guide is +5% q/q): 17.2 x 1.03^2 = $18.25B.

Q3 actual 20,095/29,591 = 67.9%; Q4 guide ~66% with gross margin ~73% vs 78% a year ago (rack/XPU mix). Incremental margin Q3->Q4 = (0.66 x 34.8 - 20.095)/(34.8 - 29.591) = 55.2%; applying it to FY28 growth gives (91.9 + 0.552 x (231.5 - 139.2))/231.5 = 61.7%. Management's '>$30' at $230B AI implies ~63%. 62% sits between.

Q3 non-GAAP interest expense $703M x 4; other income ignored, which is conservative (citation gate: other income, net of $98M is shown in the 8-K non-GAAP reconciliation [1]; leaving it out is the agent's choice, not a sourcing gap).
Q4 non-GAAP diluted share count guide, held flat (buybacks assumed to offset dilution).
Revenue 177 + 18.25 + 36.2 = $231.5B; (231.5 x 0.62 - 2.81) x (1 - 0.16 tax) / 4.94 = $23.92. Cross-check: +23% on FY27 consensus $19.39 [6]; below management's '>$30' because AI is $177B, not $230B.

Equal to AVGO's current next-FY multiple ($377.32 / $19.39 = 19.46x), i.e. the market keeps today's ~18% discount to the 11-peer next-FY median (23.66x). Inside the peer range (15.3x-60.9x), between NVDA 15.32x and TSM 21.84x and below the large-cap cohort median (NVDA, CSCO, TSM, AMD: 21.3x). Discount persists for verified reasons: six XPU customers of which 'four ... are just simply going to be huge' [2], and Broadcom's customer-financing exposure ($29B max backstop + $42B undrawn convertible-note facility [4]). No further discount: peers growing +28-31% next year (TSM, ADI, ANET) trade 21.8x-40.8x, so FY28 growth of +23% does not justify going below today's 19.5x.

methods.inputs: Equity FCF/share FY28 $19.97, FY29 $23.97 (+20%), FY30 $26.36 (+10%), FY31 $27.68 (+5%), terminal growth 3%, discount rate 12%; valued at the Oct-2027 horizon

inputs_detail.input: FCF conversion of non-GAAP net income
inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 FY26 FCF $13,665M / non-GAAP net income $16,372M = 0.835.
House base 2028 capex growth 2,255/1,841 - 1 = +22.5%; revisions are pro-cyclical (Meta 2023 -23%), so fade toward GDP-plus. Unchanged from round 1.
10y Treasury 5.31% (2026-10-05) + 5Y beta 1.48 x 4.5% equity risk premium (ERP is judgment) = 11.97% -> 12%.
Below the 5.31% nominal 10y; conservative for a cyclical semis franchise.

bear.story: AI capex digestion: house low case has 2028 capex ($1,265B) below 2027 ($1,390B) [20], so FY28 AI ~ 115 x 1,265/1,390 = $104.7B; revenue $159.1B at 60% margin -> EPS $15.76; P/E 14x (below every large-cap peer, as earnings would be falling) = $220.6; DCF with 5/5/3% growth = $151.2; blend 0.6/0.4 = $192.8. A financing event on the first tranche (up to $29B backstop, $42B facility [4]) would sit here. Cisco 2000-01 fell ~78-80% in 12 months in the vendor-financing bust [18][19], the extreme version of this path.

base.story: FY27 AI ~$115B delivered, FY28 tracking ~$177B (7.85% of house base capex): EPS $23.92 x 19x = $454.5, DCF $274.6, blend $382.5. This is the fair value.

bull.story: Management's $230B FY28 is met (house high capex case $3,160B [20]; 2024-26 capex drift was always up): revenue $284.5B at 63% -> EPS $29.99 (~management's '>$30' [2]); P/E 22x (~TSM 21.84x, below the 23.66x peer median) = $659.9; DCF with 25/12/6% growth = $366.1; blend $542.3.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Base-rate stance: assume the market keeps its current discount rather than forecasting a re-rating. The discount is persistent for verified structural reasons, not sell-side calls: (1) concentration: six XPU customers, four of them 'huge' [2]; (2) Broadcom carries customer-financing exposure: up to $29B undiscounted backstop on the first (Anthropic, ~1 GW) tranche plus a $42B uncommitted convertible-note facility, $0 drawn [4], with later tranches not sized; (3) the market already applies this discount to the mega-cap AI-silicon cohort (NVDA 15.32x). No premium is claimed, and no discount beyond today's is applied, because +28-31% growers (TSM, ADI, ANET) trade at 21.8x-40.8x.

thesis_break_reason: 13.7x FY27 consensus EPS ($19.39 [6]) and 8.6% below the 52-week low ($289.96 on 2026-03-30 [17]). Trading there would mean the market no longer believes the supply-secured ~$115B FY27 AI revenue [2]: a cut at the 2026-12-09 or March print, a lab customer deferring GW deployments, a lease default that triggers the up-to-$29B backstop [4], or a 2027-28 capex cut toward the house low case [20]. That is a fundamental break, not 47%-vol noise.

Fundamentals: Q3 FY26 revenue $29.6B, non-GAAP op margin 67.9%, FCF conversion 0.835 [1]; Q4 guide $34.8B at ~66% [1][2]; FY27 AI ~$115B secured, FY28 'line of sight' $230B, EPS '>$30' [2]; FY27 consensus $19.39 [6]. FY28 AI = mean of three anchors ($140.9B constant capex share [20], $159.3B commitment ratio [3], $230B management [2]) = $177B -> EPS $23.92. Prediction markets as context only: recession by end-2026 7.0% [10], Taiwan by end-2027 11.5% [13], 'AI bubble burst' by mid-2027 17.5% (thin) [11]. Ladder = 0.75 x scenario mixture (lognormal residuals 0.30/0.24/0.27 around $193/$382/$542) + 0.25 x lognormal(median $382.5, sigma 0.47); median ~$376, mean ~$397; overall log-sd ~0.46 matches realised vol.
